title: Engagement-to-Renewal Likelihood — Sandbox Scoring Worksheet
summary: Sandbox worksheet for building an "_engagement-to-renewal' composite score. Focused on short-term trajectory signals (last 30–90d), friction indicators, and a simple probabilistic mapping to renewal likelihood for use in QBR narratives and playbook triggers.
scoring_overview: Goal: produce a 0–100 Renewal Likelihood score that combines: (A) recent trajectory (slope of core usage metrics), (B) friction signals (support volume, errors, latency regressions), (C) adoption breadth (number of active routes/integrations), and (D) qualitative CS inputs. This sheet is intentionally experimental — contains multiple weighting permutations and calibration notes for A/B comparison in QBRs.
signals_table:
Signals (raw features) and quick transform notes:
- API-active-days-30d: count of days with >=1 successful token generation call in the past 30 days. (norm -> 0–1 by dividing by 30)
- median-response-latency-14d: median p95 latency across production routes (ms). (inverse log transform)
- kv-cache-hit-rate-7d: fraction of requests hit cache. (use as multiplier to indicate efficiency)
- routes-active: distinct API routes used in last 90d. (cap at 20)
- embeddings-batch-size-mean: proxy for advanced usage patterns (bigger batches -> power users)
- support-tickets-30d: count tagged 'regression' or 'latency'. (decay window, recent tickets weighted more)
- canary-fallback-count: automatic fallbacks fired in last 30d (reliability loss signal)
- pricing-plan-change: boolean (downgrade=strong negative)
- dedicated-adoption: fraction of traffic on Dedicated vs Hosted (higher Dedicated typically higher stickiness)
- eval-regression-alerts-90d: count of quality regression alerts against customer prompt-suite
Transforms: all numeric signals standardized per-customer percentiles (rolling baseline), then mapped to 0–1 via clamped sigmoid for tail robustness.
risk_flag_logic:
Quick rule-based flags we surfaced during the sandbox (not final):
- RED: support-tickets-30d >= 4 OR canary-fallback-count >= 3 OR pricing-plan-change == downgrade
- AMBER: API-active-days-30d < 6 AND routes-active <= 1
- GREEN: API-active-days-30d >= 18 AND eval-regression-alerts-90d == 0 AND dedicated-adoption >= 0.6
These flags overlay the continuous Renewal Likelihood score for playbook triage (RED -> high-touch CS + immediate incident review).
weighting_experiments:
Experiment matrix (columns are experiments we want to compare in a cohort-based A/B):
1) Usage-first: 50% trajectory, 20% friction, 20% breadth, 10% qualitative
2) Reliability-first: 30% trajectory, 40% friction, 20% breadth, 10% qualitative
3) Breadth-boost: 35% trajectory, 20% friction, 35% breadth, 10% qualitative
Calibration approach: map raw composite to probability via isotonic regression against historical renewal labels (18–24mo rolling window). Evaluate Brier score, calibration plots, and top-decile lift. Track per-cohort (SMB, Mid-market, Enterprise) separately.
action_playbook:
Automated actions tied to score bands and flags:
- Score >= 85 & GREEN: Auto-schedule QBR + invite Solutions Eng for expansion conversation; mark for 'advocacy' touchpoint.
- Score 60–84 & AMBER: Trigger Health Outreach sequence (2-week nurture + usage nudges), schedule solutions review if routes-active doesn't grow.
- Score < 60 or RED: Escalation to AE + CS leader; require incident postmortem for any reliability flag; propose 30-day retention offer (technical or commercial) if downgrade risk persists.
Playbook notes: include templated Slack messages, a JIRA incident stub, and a checklist for SE to validate model signals (false-positive guardrails).
next_steps:
1) Run scoring on last 6 months of customers -> produce cohort calibration report (target: Brier < 0.19 for mid-market).
2) Instrument dashboards for top contributing signals per customer (so CS can validate before outreach).
3) Pilot Experiment 2 (Reliability-first) on 150 high-ARR accounts; measure retention at 90d post-touch.
4) Add structured CS qualitative score (0–10) from QBR notes and retrain monthly.
5) Create a lightweight endpoint in CS tooling to fetch 'score rationale' (top 3 signals driving score) for transparency.
notes_to_self:
- This is a sandbox: expect noisy labels, especially for newly onboarded customers.
- Watch out for seasonality (billing cycle end dates spike engagement).
- Consider a separate model for Dedicated customers due to different inertia.
- Keep the playbook template in repo and link in QBR slide deck.
- Add a short survey trigger for accounts with sudden drop in 'routes_active' to validate signal origin (product change vs customer churn).
